model_annotation: This bar chart illustrates the negative log probability of Mistralv0.2-Base when fine-tuned on six medical specialties—Cardio, Gastro, Infect, Neuro, Obstetrics, and Pediatrics—evaluated against per-specialty terms. The vertical axis represents “Negative log probability,” ranging from approximately -27 to -22, with lower values indicating higher model confidence. Each specialty is represented by a group of six bars (one for each fine-tuning domain), color-coded according to the legend: light blue for Cardio, light orange for Gastro, medium orange for Infect, dark orange for Neuro, brown for Obstetrics, and dark brown for Pediatrics. The horizontal axis lists the evaluation domains (“Per-specialty terms”), with each group showing how the model performs when fine-tuned on different specialties. In general, the model achieves the best (lowest) negative log probability when fine-tuned on the same specialty it is evaluated on (e.g., Cardio fine-tuned on Cardio terms), as indicated by the tallest bars within each group. Performance degrades when the model is evaluated on specialties different from its fine-tuning domain, with cross-specialty evaluations typically showing higher (worse) negative log probabilities. The chart visually emphasizes that domain-specific fine-tuning improves performance on in-domain terms, with the most pronounced drops in performance observed for Infect and Neuro when evaluated outside their respective domains.
